apps.name: DroneDeploy Flight App
apps.releaseNotes:
New Features

  - RTK connect in flight — Drones can now connect to RTK mid-flight by pausing at the first waypoint, suspending, then resuming
  - Starting waypoint offset slider — New planning UI control to calibrate the starting waypoint position on long flight legs
  - Terrain Awareness — Expanded acreage limit for terrain awareness missions
  - Flight log timestamps — Timestamps now shown alongside entries in the timeline viewer

  Improvements

  - Firmware alerts — Only flags firmware that is genuinely older than required, reducing false update prompts
  - Camera display names — All supported cameras now show human-readable names throughout the app
  - Travel altitude — Resets automatically when switching back to automatic altitude settings
  - RTK stability — Consolidated connection paths and prompts drone reset when RTK datum changes mid-connection
  - Mission reliability — Flight path changes are now applied synchronously; numeric values in mission JSON rounded to prevent floating-point drift

  Bug Fixes

  - App startup & navigation — Fixed 60-second startup delay on legacy-auth devices and unsigned sessions; fixed invisible text on the active mobile
  nav tab
  - Missions & planning — Fixed geofence RTH marked as failed when all waypoints completed; fixed image count using stale data after flight path
  changes; fixed non-resumable missions appearing in the queue; fixed approach waypoint heading
  - Capture — Fixed pano missions capturing half the expected photos on thermal drones; fixed Progress Video recording before the gimbal reached its
  planned angle
  - Stand assessment — Fixed markers not loading, gimbal angle on first photo, and PDF reports downloading as 0 bytes
  - Map & visualization — Fixed FPV view maximizing to map instead of camera from vertical layout; fixed wrong direction in aircraft detection
  messages

apps.name: ARK: Survival Ascended
Rust
apps.releaseNotes:
PRINTED AND POLISHED

BLUEPRINT REWORK

Workbenches no longer require blueprint fragments to craft, and scrap isn’t used on the tech trees. Instead, we’re introducing three tiers of blueprints; blueprint fragments, blueprint pages and blueprint books. These are the new currencies spent to progress tech trees. One for each tech tree level.

Items can still be researched with scrap on the research table. There is a much greater emphasis on finding, trading for, or making allies to get items you need. This part of Rust was somewhat lost along the way.

The overarching theme for this overhaul is shifting the difficulty. The previous blueprint fragment system caused a lot of friction in the early game progression, especially for players with less time on their hands. Due to the spawn locations of basic fragments, transitioning to a Workbench level 2 could be a difficult task. If you couldn’t compete, you weren’t just slowed down, you were locked out. The lowest tier blueprint can now be found in common loot sources such as barrels and boxes, but most importantly can be upgraded into the next tier of blueprint. Puzzle rooms and harder content will still be the fastest way to progress.

Workbench upgrades which affected scrap used on the tech tree have also been reworked. Instead of reducing the amount of scrap used, the salvage workbench upgrade now has a 20% chance to not consume a blueprint. The prototype workbench upgrade will now be a flat 25% success rate, with the cost doubling removed.

We don’t know exactly how this will play out, and we’d be kidding ourselves to think we’ve got it perfect on the first iteration. Adjustments will be made when needed and we certainly won’t wait as long as last time when that time comes.

UZI 9MM

Introducing the iconic new UZI 9mm Submachine Gun. This weapon offers two different firing modes depending on stock configuration. When folded, the weapon is automatic and compatible with shields. When unfolded, the Uzi becomes semi-automatic and gains increased accuracy.

Hold the fire mode button to switch between them.

GAMEPAD SUPPORT

Gamepad support has arrived in Rust, with controller functionality now available across the core gameplay via Steam Input.

The inventory and crafting UI is handled via a stick cursor by default, but there's a D-pad toggle in the new gamepad options screen, which is definitely worth trying out! You can find a bunch of other settings there too, to tweak the feel of the gamepad.

This first release brings a pretty solid experience already, but not every feature or functionality will have dedicated gamepad support yet. I'll continue to add additional support over time, so if there's something in particular you feel is missing, let us know!

LIVESTOCK REWORK

This patch the focus has been on making livestock more intuitive and less punishing.

•
You are now simply the owner of the cow if you buy it or have it eat at your trough, no need to stay near the cow or be worried it'll forget you anymore except for leading.
[/*]
•
Cows don't die of old age anymore, and instead of dying of starvation just lie down at 1 hp.
[/*]
•
How long a trough can sustain a group of cows is now shown in the trough UI similar to upkeep.
[/*]
•
Cows can now eat any food a horse can.
[/*]
•
Overgrazing "grazed bare" is gone. Having enough grass in your pen will simply cause cows to eat at the trough twice less often and save on food.
[/*]
•
Show everything in the UI, owner, pregnancy status father and cooldown, dung and milk/wool cooldown...
[/*]
•
Cows will store up to 3 milk to reduce micromanagement.
[/*]
•
Hint at recessive genes with the UI and the NPC buyer, also hint at them in the UI.
[/*]
•
Personal space need is simplified, it just measures the area of the pen and check if enough cows can fit, it should not fluctuate as much and we should have the same value for the whole herd.

•
Free range owned cows stop reproducing past 6, indoor cows stop reproducing when there is not enough…

apps.name: Dota 2
apps.releaseNotes:
Inside the Trove of Terror

Some time ago, a time now none of us can quite recall, we began to set our minds on matters of the monstrous. Our work has always concerned itself with the manufacture of frightening things, so there was no reason at that time for alarm.

Until we began to fill a new treasure chest with item sets themed around eldritch and otherworldly designs.

As each horrific creation took more defined shape, unsettling yet tantalizing inspirations took hold of us. Fantastical and Immortal glamours coalesced around each and every set; they grew more spellbinding, a vision that would remain, stuck fast in the mind's eye. Thoughts of monsters birthed thoughts of even more monstrous monsters. Our minds became gateways for greater abominations still, our hands became not our own.

Soon our collection of new item sets numbered fifteen, eldritch abominations from the realm of nightmare all. We knew each thing was hideous. Not one of us could look away. Not one of us was content to stop there.

To master horrors, we required greater horrors... We required ARCANA.

Our first attempt summoned the haunting shape of a Drow Ranger Arcana long thought lost to the flow of time. By some trick of the mind, she can look as she once did or assume a grave-stalking new form.

Our appetites remained unsatisfied.

Our second attempt unleashed something none of us had ever seen, something that hungrily emerged from a bloodstained sea: the all-new Maw of the Megalodon Arcana for the creature called Tidehunter, arriving with a new model, a host of custom animations, effects, taunts, voice lines, and dragging a familiar-looking corpse that serves as one part security blanket and one part snack. A whisper in the darkness, instructing, teasing: "Should one master this Arcana's secrets, one would surely unlock all three of its shark-toothed designs."

This Trove is a doorway to things we cannot explain, let alone understand. The more of these treasures that you open, the more your own minds shine out like beacons to things lurking beyond the limits of reason. Open enough treasures and you're guaranteed to attract the gaze of an all-seeing new Tormentor. Open a number more and you'll surely summon the face of eldritch terror itself, manifesting as an incomprehensible new design for Roshan.

We must part now with one final revelation. Take it as a warning if you wish. We didn't make this treasure... It made itself. We thought we were creating something, but we were not. We were merely the conduit, unknowingly letting something into our world from the great dark beyond: The Trove of Terror — overflowing with a mind-bending number of Immortal item sets, one new and one returning Arcana, and brand-new Tormentor and Roshan appearances — available now.

If you dare, all you need to do is launch Dota to learn more.

apps.name: Mozilla Firefox (en-US)
apps.releaseNotes:
Version 160.0, first offered to Release channel users on November 10, 2026

New
- The Picture-in-Picture player now has a playback speed setting, with options ranging from 0.25x to 2.0x speed. The setting appears only when the player window is medium-sized or larger.

- Mini Window moves a tab or a selected part of a page into an always-on-top window while browsing. We’d appreciate feedback on Mozilla Connect as we develop and improve this early version of the feature.

- History entries can now be dragged from the sidebar to the tab strip to open them in new tabs.
- The address bar context menu now shows "Paste and Search" instead of "Paste and Go" when the copied text is a search term rather than a web address.
- Pages saved as PDF now make mathematical content (MathML) accessible to assistive technology such as screen readers.
- Websites that repeatedly ask to handle email (mailto:) and other links can now be blocked with a new “Never allow” button, and blocked sites can be managed in Settings.
- Firefox now plays Matroska (MKV) files with FLAC, MP3, or PCM audio.
- WebGL content on macOS is now rendered using Apple's Metal graphics API, which can improve performance on some sites.
- In Smart Window, Organize Tabs is now available in French. Firefox can suggest groups of related open tabs and name each group in French.
  This feature is part of a progressive roll out.
  What is a progressive roll out?
  Certain new Firefox features are released gradually. This means some users will see the feature before everyone does. This approach helps to get early feedback to catch bugs and improve behavior quickly, meaning more Firefox users overall have a better experience.

Fixed
- Fixed the first character typed into the address bar or search bar sometimes being lost when typing quickly right after clicking into it.
- Increased the contrast between the domain name and the rest of the address in the address bar, making it easier to see which website is open.
- Fixed Firefox freezing for several seconds when signing in to intranet sites that use NTLM or Kerberos (Negotiate) authentication.
- Fixed double-tapping or long-pressing a word to select it, and tapping to place the cursor, not working near the cursor in text fields.
- Fixed links opened in the background from other apps on macOS, such as RSS readers, bringing Firefox to the foreground.
- Fixed downloaded files on macOS sometimes opening in the wrong application instead of the default one set in Finder.
- Fixed simultaneous downloads on macOS never finishing when Firefox is set to ask where to save files. Only the first file showed a save dialog.
- Restored meaningful filenames and the usual save workflow for PDFs opened in Preview from the macOS print dialog.
- Various security fixes.

Enterprise
- For Firefox Enterprise updates and fixes, see the Firefox Enterprise Release Notes. For policy changes, see the Firefox admin docs changelog.

Developer

Web Platform
- The SpeechRecognition interface of the Web Speech API is now supported, providing on-device, real-time speech-to-text in 40 languages.
- Firefox now supports the legacy ::-webkit-input-placeholder pseudo-element as an alias of ::placeholder, to improve compatibility with websites that use it to style placeholder text.

Community Contributions
- With the release of Firefox 160, we are pleased to welcome the developers who contributed their first code change to Firefox in this release, 22 of whom were brand new volunteers!
